title: Schema and Item Modeling
readerIntent: Understand how Nodics turns business concepts into governed, provider-independent data contracts.
owner: Owning business modules plus Nodics schema and data-model capabilities
summary: A schema defines a business record once; Nodics builds the corresponding item-model behavior and delegates persistence through configured database contracts.

sections.heading: Business value
items: Use consistent business definitions across APIs, workflows, imports, search, and BackOffice.
Change supported database providers without moving business ownership into an adapter.
Express relationships, tenant boundaries, access policy, validation, indexing, and versioning intent as governed metadata.
Extend customer-specific fields through layered modules instead of copying the original model.

sections.heading: Schema, item model, and search model
items: The schema is the authoritative structural and behavioral contract owned by a capability.
The item model represents authoritative record operations through the Nodics data framework.
The search model represents query and index behavior for schemas that enable search.
Neither a business service nor a frontend should bypass these contracts to access a database or search engine directly.
